If anyone has gained momentum after the pandemic, it’s the eCommerce industry. According to [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/indian-e-commerce-to-grow-84-in-4-years-helped-by-covid-19-impact-study-121031000846_1.html), it is believed that India’s e-commerce industry will grow 84 percent (to $111 billion) by 2024, due to covid’s impact worldwide.

So, to handle the humongous data related to inventory, fulfillment, vendors, shipping, returns, and many more activities that entail the D2C supply chain, online retailers are now adapting to [Unicommerce](https://unicommerce.com/), a leader in supply chain management through product lifecycles.

This blog covers how markets are working with unicommerce now, and how [Datachannel’s](https://datachannel.co/) new integration can help you optimize your ROI.

## How does Unicommerce Platform Work?

Unicommerce is a supply chain Saas platform, that provides sellers with automated data related to inventory, sales, shipping, returns, accounting, and much more. This helps brands connect with their target audiences and have maximum reach. With 15000+ brands in its marketplace, Unicommerce has proven to reduce operational costs, pinpoint top-selling products, and optimize omnichannel sales. This technology giant handles approximately 1.3 billion transactions every day, advocating for “hassle-free business”.  Some of its key clients are Myntra, Adidas, Vero Moda, Chumbak, W for women, House of Anita Dongre, Marico, Netmeds, Healthkart, mCaffeine, Sugar Cosmetics, Lakme, and Nivea.

The Unicommerce platform provides for:

1.  Warehouse management
2.  Order management
3.  Inventory management
4.  Omnichannel retailing
5.  Vendor panel management
6.  Returns management

Since data is gathered from multiple tools and apps within Unicommerce, information is often scattered, and is prone to cause [silos.](https://datachannel.co/blogs/data-silos-to-automated-insights-uncover-marketing-potential/) This especially applies when you’re pulling data from multiple apps (Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Shopify, etc) within the platform. The ultimate fall down is the inability to find insights that let you move further in your business, or increase your ROI.

## How Can This Data Be Used To Drive Business Growth?

Consolidate your data: Just having a lot of data coming in doesn’t drive growth. One needs to know how to use it for different purposes. That’s why e-sellers are now focusing on consolidating this data, [transforming it in warehouses](https://datachannel.co/blogs/data-transformation-can-deliver-better-insights-for-saas-marketers/); essentially making it “*usable”*, and analyzing it for various use cases.

-   Keep an eye on eCommerce trends: With digital advancements, e-retailers now have access to [new tools](https://datachannel.co/blogs/trending-etl-tools-2022/) that boost business productivity. Keeping up with what apps competitors are using for data storage, accessibility and visualization is a must.
-   Work towards customer satisfaction: having loyal customers is always a plus, and data helps you figure out where you can direct your ops teams to get more repeat purchases. Not only this, but the correct data will also help you personalize your ads and marketing strategy, letting you target different sets of audiences appropriately, and resulting in better sales.
-   Automate your reports: With automation at every step, automated reports have proven to provide clearer insights. When inefficiencies in data are removed, automated reports enable better decision-making, which helps organizations in the long run.
